_comment: Copy this beside your working files, then edit. Every flat-rate value here is a placeholder. A provider type of 'none' means NO PROVIDER IS AVAILABLE for that leg — never use it to switch off a field the installer is not interested in. What gets attempted is decided per record by the skip flags at run time, so give every field a provider can reach a leg. An http leg names `key_env`, the environment variable holding that provider's key — no credential ever goes in this file. A leg's `skip` names the caller opt-out that switches it off; omit `skip` for an ENABLING lookup that should run only when a leg downstream requires its field. Every deepline_tool / deepline_play id below was confirmed with `deepline tools describe` / `deepline plays describe` (2026-09).
name: Contact enrichment cascade
_comment_tuning: All three below are optional and shown at their defaults.

legs._comment: An ENABLING lookup that can also be requested. It carries `want` (opt-IN, default off) rather than `skip`, because it exists for the legs after it rather than for its own sake — it fires whenever something downstream requires a domain, and otherwise only when a caller asks with want_company_domain. crustdata_v3_company_enrich takes `names` as an array, so the field is written as a one-item list. 0.8 Deepline credits per result.

A flat-rate provider that finds the pivot from name + company. This is the valuable shape: it lands BEFORE the pivot and unlocks every leg that needs a profile URL. generic_http_request returns the provider body under `data`.
The credit-billed pivot finder: a Deepline waterfall play. Paying for the profile URL here is what turns the flat-rate email and phone legs behind it from unreachable to free.
Flat-rate email, keyed off the pivot. `requires` is what makes this SKIP rather than fire and die when the pivot was never found.

A GET provider: query parameters rather than a JSON body. The KEY is the provider's own parameter name (theirs, from their spec) and the VALUE is our record field. A Bearer-style provider sets key_header Authorization and key_prefix 'Bearer '.
The credit-billed fallback: Deepline's email waterfall play. It runs only when every flat-rate leg above came back empty, which is the one boundary where cost-ascending ordering actually saves money.

Phone is usually the dearest field — and the leg is still built. It fires only on a record that wants a phone and whose free lookup missed, and skip_phone stops it entirely. prebuilt/person-to-phone needs only a name; the LinkedIn URL and domain are passed when known.

Verification reports, it never rewrites. The address is always emitted; the verdict decides whether contact_email_verified_only is populated. zerobounce_validate, 0.28 Deepline credits per result; catch-all comes back as status catch-all and is not in verified_statuses.

_comment_enabler: Every field a provider can reach gets a leg, and every leg carries a skip flag so a caller can both request and suppress it per record. A leg still fires when a downstream leg REQUIRES its field, flag or no flag — otherwise the downstream leg could never run. Omit `skip` entirely only for a field nobody should ever be able to request.
